🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Donnie Dunagan, the child actor who gave young Bambi his voice in Walt Disney's 1942 animated classic Bambi, has died at 92.

Dunagan died Wednesday, November 4, 2026, of lung cancer, author and film historian Tom Weaver reported. The Hollywood Reporter published his obituary on Monday, November 9, 2026.

Dunagan was born Donald Roan Dunagan on August 16, 1934, in San Antonio, Texas, and grew up in Memphis, Tennessee. He came to Hollywood as a small boy after talent scouts spotted him tap dancing, and he made seven films as a child actor. He played the young Peter Frankenstein in Son of Frankenstein (1939) alongside Boris Karloff and Basil Rathbone, appeared in Tower of London (1939), and then took on the role that would define him: the voice of the young fawn in Bambi. Walt Disney himself called Dunagan's mother to offer him the part. Bambi was his seventh and last film.

He walked away from Hollywood at 18 and joined the United States Marine Corps, serving for 25 years without telling his fellow Marines about his past in the movies. He earned three Purple Hearts and a Bronze Star and retired with the rank of major in 1977.

Film historians tracked him down in 2004, and his story — the boy who voiced Bambi and then kept it a secret through a decorated military career — reached a much wider audience. More than 70 years after recording Bambi, he finally met Peter Behn, the voice of Thumper, and Stan Alexander, the voice of Flower.

Dunagan is survived by his wife, Dana, whom he married in 1992.

Rest in Peace, Donnie Dunagan.

Sources: The Hollywood Reporter (obituary by Mike Barnes, November 9, 2026, citing film historian Tom Weaver); Parade; The A.V. Club.

title: Beyond the 956: Donnie Dunagan, the original voice of Bambi, dies at 92
